title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly check-in for the Redwood Private (VPC) pilot. Reviewed networking progress (VPC peering, route tables), routing to private subnets, validation of TLS/KMS integration, performance baseline after kernel upgrade, and plan for next week to complete SOC2 artefact exchange and run the 10k-record latency benchmark.
topics: Model runtime upgrade (v2.3 -> v2.4) and kernel selection
action_items: Alex: Send updated network diagram + security checklist (by 2027-10-10)
Priya: Share exact kernel build and runtime flags used for v2.4 test (by 2027-10-08)
Maya: Confirm subnet NAT gateway and route table entries, attach screenshots (by 2027-10-09)
Liam: Provide SOC2 A3 artefact location and point of contact (by 2027-10-12)
next_steps: Redwood to schedule on-site dry-run for certificate rotation (target week of 2027-10-18)
Customer to run 10k-record inference benchmark with provided load script and share results (target 2027-10-15)
Exchange final SAML metadata and validate SSO in staging (target 2027-10-14)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Redwood), Jared Thompson (Atlas Health CTO), Maya Patel (Atlas DevOps), Liam O'Connor (Atlas Security), Sofia Ruiz (Atlas ML)

Summary (auto): Weekly pilot sync to review network gating items, confirm the runtime upgrade results, and plan the SOC2/doc exchange.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Jared: Jared here.
[00:06] Maya: Maya.
[00:07] Liam: Liam.
[00:08] Sofia: hi, sofia.
[00:10] Priya: Priya from Redwood. Marco also on.

[00:30] Alex: Cool. Agenda — network status, runtime upgrade results from Priya, security items from Liam, then wrap with next steps.

[02:05] Maya: quick update from our side — we finished the VPC peering yesterday, but traffic to the private inference subnet was still failing until we adjusted the route table for the peered CIDR. so that seems fixed now, we also opened up the security group to allow 8443 from the redwood control-plane ip. there was a transient issue with the NAT gateway that dropped some egress, but that was ephemeral.

[03:20] Priya: ok that matches what we saw. when we tried to hit the agent, we got TLS handshake errors initially because the cert chain on the customer side was missing the intermediate cert. once maya pushed the full chain it's clean. the agent also needed the route-table entry to the private ENI — otherwise our health checks timed out.

[04:15] Jared: yeah that was on me, i forgot to attach the intermediate in the initial cert. my bad.

[05:00] Marco: small note — in some of our logs the product name shows as "Redwood Privatee" with two e's in the autogen which confused our parser. not a blocker but FYI.

[06:30] Priya: moving to runtime — we ran the v2.4 runtime w/ the new kernel flags (continuous batching on, kv-cache pruning at 1000 entries) and saw a median p95 token latency drop of ~12% compared to v2.3 baseline. throughput at 8 concurrent clients increased about 18%. numbers are on the spreadsheet i shared.

[07:05] Sofia: can you repeat the exact kernel flags? the ops team needs to pin them if we upgrade staging.

[07:20] Priya: sure — flags were: --batching=continuous, --kv-prune=1000, --fp16-quant (we used int8xx for one run but results were noisier). i'll paste exact flags after the call.

[08:00] Maya: we tried int8 quantization on the model variant and saw a small quality regression in the ner tasks; so we held off for now because that impacts triage.

[08:30] Priya: yes that's expected; quantization tradeoffs vary by workload. for embeddings and rerank tasks int8 was fine, for NER you might see token-level errors. we can run a mixed profile where generation uses fp16 and embeddings use int8.

[09:15] Liam: security — quick status. we got the initial SOC2 snapshot you requested, but i need the exact list of audit logs Redwood stores. can you confirm retention period and whether logs include token-level metadata?

[09:40] Alex: good question. we retain operational logs 90 days by default, audit logs for access events 180 days under the pilot config; token-level raw content is not stored unless customer enables it — by default we store metadata and truncated hashes. i'll send the doc link.

[10:20] Liam: and KMS — are we bringing our KMS keys or using Redwood-managed?

[10:30] Priya: for the Private deployment you can bring your KMS (we integrate via customer KMS with keywrap). in staging we integrated with Atlas KMS and validated envelope encryption during the run. the cert rotation path works but we'll do a dry-run with your ops team.

[11:00] Maya: ops question — when we did the kernel upgrade we noticed occasional OOMs on pods pinned with 24GB memory during high concurrency. any tuning tips?

[11:25] Priya: two things — the new runtime is more memory-aggressive because of prefetching; increase the pod memory to 28-32GB or reduce batch size. also enable the kv-cache prune more aggressively for long seqs.

[12:10] Sofia: do you have sample auto-scaling policy recommendations? we're worried about cold-start latency with autoscale.

[12:30] Marco: recommendation — keep a small warm pool of 2-3 reserved GPUs on Dedicated or in Private you can keep standby pods with preloaded weights; shorten cold-start by snapshotting KV cache to shared volume if your workload has many repeated prefixes.

[13:30] Alex: can we talk about routing and fallbacks? earlier we discussed smart routing to cheaper model variants if the primary is throttled. any blockers on that in Private mode?

[13:55] Priya: routing policy works in Private as long as the control plane can hit the agent endpoints over the peered link. current peering allows that; only thing to be careful of is route overlap with existing corporate CIDR — we recommend an isolated /20 for the inference subnets.

[15:05] Maya: FYI our corporate net uses 10.1.0.0/16 so we allocated 10.2.0.0/20 for redwood. added static routes and NAT.

[15:30] Liam: on SSO — we tested SAML metadata import, login worked, but group sync failed intermittently. looks like our IdP is trimming the group attribute.

[15:50] Alex: we can add a mapping rule or fallback to LDAP attribute. Priya will help triage.

[17:00] Priya: about the benchmark — we ran 2k-record run yesterday and attached the sheet. p50 token latency 65ms, p95 220ms for the small gen workload. when we enabled the new kernel flags p95 dropped to 195ms. these runs were on a 4-GPU private pool, mixed batch, 8 concurrent clients.

[18:10] Sofia: those numbers look promising. do you expect the same improvement at scale (10k records)?

[18:30] Priya: likely similar percentage improvement but absolute numbers may increase due to tail effects. that's why we want you to run the 10k with the load script we shared.

[19:05] Jared: any change to data residency or logging with the kernel upgrade?

[19:15] Alex: no, kernel/runtime changes don't change logging defaults. KMS and logging config are independent.

[20:20] Maya: question — what's the recommended approach for cert rotation? we need a maintenance window.

[20:30] Marco: rotate certs via the operator CLI; we recommend a rolling rotation across nodes with 15 minute drain windows. we'll do a dry-run in staging first and then schedule for prod.

[21:40] Liam: also need the encryption-at-rest confirmation for snapshots and s3 backups.

[21:50] Priya: snapshots are encrypted with customer KMS. for s3 backups we encrypt server-side with customer-managed KMS keys. will include exact bucket policy snippet.

[23:00] Alex: ok let's go quick through open blockers — Maya?

[23:10] Maya: route tables and cert chain fixed. NAT glitch was transient. we still need the operator CLI tutorial to push the runtime flags.

[23:30] Priya: i'll send a short operator CLI how-to and the exact command to set flags.

[24:00] Sofia: on model quality — we need a small eval to confirm NER after int8 changes. can Redwood run an eval against our testset?

[24:20] Priya: yes we'll run a quick eval against your testset; send the dataset link or sample prompts.

[25:00] Jared: timeline — we want pilot finish in two weeks and a decision by 2027-10-28. are we aligned?

[25:15] Alex: that is our timeline too; sounds tight but doable if benchmarks and SOC2 artefacts land.

[26:10] Marco: quick note about logs surfaced in the console — cost breakdown per-token is in the console but in Private we ship that metrics collection to your prometheus endpoint; need to ensure metrics scraping is configured.

[27:00] Maya: prometheus already running in staging; i'll open a PR with scrape config.

[28:15] Priya: ok last thing — fallback policy: if primary model crosses 95% CPU we can route by label to a cheaper variant; that requires consistent model tags in your deployment.

[29:05] Liam: security sign-off — once we get the audit log list and the SOC2 artefact pointer, we can do a quick review. expected sign-off timeline 3-4 business days.

[29:40] Alex: great. recap of next steps and owners — i'll read them out.

[30:00] Alex: Alex to send network diagram + security checklist by 2027-10-10. Priya to paste kernel flags and operator CLI commands by 2027-10-08. Maya to confirm NAT/route screenshots by 2027-10-09. Liam to share SOC2 artefact location by 2027-10-12. Redwood to run NER eval when dataset provided. Customer to run 10k benchmark by 2027-10-15. Schedule cert rotation dry-run week of 2027-10-18.

[31:10] Jared: sounds good.

[31:20] Maya: one more tiny ask — can you share the CPU/GPU utilization template you use for sizing?

[31:30] Marco: yes will attach template.

[33:00] Alex: ok if no more questions we'll wrap. thanks everyone.

[33:05] Sofia: thanks all.

[33:10] Pria: thanks (note - minor typo in transcript: Pria -> Priya)

[33:20] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript has minor autocaption errors and occasional speaker mislabels; see action items for definitive owners.
